clue.text: Oswald's assassinated — if it can go wrong it will?

definitions.text: if it can go wrong it will?

indicators.note: a killing violently destroys the name, so the letters of the assassin's name are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: the name Oswald with its possessive S, all seven letters used

explanation.surface: A grim headline about Lee Harvey Oswald's death, tacked onto a weary remark about bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the 'S counts as a letter: the anagram uses all seven letters of OSWALDS.
explanation.definitionFit: This British name for the principle that anything that can go wrong will is the local equivalent of Murphy's law.

clue.text: Plant accuses America, centrally

indicators.note: the letters are taken from the middle of the phrase, with its outer letters left off

explanation.surface: A mole planted in the system points the finger at the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centrally' signals that the answer sits in the middle of 'accuses America': acCUSES AMErica.
explanation.definitionFit: This oil-seed herb is a flowering crop, so it is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Randomly draw lots, mostly after 8

indicators.note: the shortened word for lots is placed after the letter from 8

parts.note: the answer to 8 down is a member of a US party, abbreviated to its initial D

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, with its final letter dropped

parts.note: oodles means lots, a great many

explanation.surface: Instructions for picking straws at random after eight o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims the last letter of OODLES to give OODLE; 'after' places that behind D, the usual abbreviation of the party name at 8 down.
explanation.definitionFit: To scribble idly without purpose is to sketch aimlessly, which matches drawing at random.

clue.text: Deputy picked up socialist resident

indicators.note: something picked up is heard, so the phrase is said aloud and its sound gives the spelling

parts.note: a socialist is on the left, and a resident is a tenant; together they are said as left-tenant

explanation.surface: An assistant overheard saying something about a left-wing householder.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English the rank is pronounced 'lef-tenant', so LEFT (socialist) plus TENANT (resident) sounds like it.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank's original meaning is someone who holds a place on behalf of a superior, a substitute or second-in-command.

clue.text: Writer's lost time working for one on the Telegraph

indicators.note: the remaining letters are worked into a new order
the writer has lost something, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: the word writer, with 's read as 'has'

explanation.surface: A journalist on the Daily Telegraph newspaper running out of time to file copy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' removes T from WRITER, leaving WRIER, which 'working' rearranges. The Telegraph here is the old wire-telegraph system, not the British newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who sends messages by wire, or installs wiring, works on the telegraph network.

clue.text: Withheld, subject to FBI man framing American

parts.note: re means on the subject of, concerning

indicators.note: the agent's word surrounds the other piece like a frame

parts.note: a Fed is a US federal agent, such as an FBI officer
US is short for American, as in United States

explanation.surface: Information held back from an American suspect who is being set up by an FBI agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something declined or not granted has been kept back, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Confusion around one's family — one of several that got JFK?

definitions.text: one of several that got JFK?

indicators.note: the word for confusion goes around the family word

parts.note: a riot is a scene of confusion and disorder
your own flesh and blood is your family

explanation.surface: Chaos surrounding a family, linked to the shots fired at Kennedy in Dallas.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: Kennedy was killed by gunfire from a long gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Kennedy was killed by bullets fired from a long gun, each being a discharge of that weapon.

clue.text: Two presidents in one, JFK was shot

parts.note: Gerald Ford was the 38th US president
Abraham Lincoln was the 16th US president, himself assassinated

explanation.surface: Linking two US presidents to the car in which Kennedy was shot.
explanation.walkthrough: Kennedy was riding in a Lincoln Continental convertible, a car made by the Ford Motor Company, when he was shot in Dallas.
explanation.definitionFit: The make of the open-topped limousine carrying the president through Dallas was a Lincoln, the luxury marque owned by Ford.

clue.text: Removing end and firing gun over president's head

indicators.note: the shooting word goes over, covering, the president's initial

parts.note: sniping is shooting from a hidden position

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A sniper shooting at a president's head, recalling the Kennedy assassination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' gives P from 'president's', and 'over' places SNIPING around it: SNIP(P)ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting off the tips of something with scissors is trimming it, taking an end off.

clue.text: Hit 25 with single round only, getting JFK?

indicators.note: something hit is knocked about, so the letters are rearranged
a round is the letter O; keeping only one of the two Os means one is removed

parts.note: the answer to 25 across is a procession of cars

explanation.surface: A sniper striking the procession with one bullet to get the president.
explanation.walkthrough: MOTORCADE has two Os; 'with single round only' removes one, leaving MTORCADE, which 'Hit' rearranges. 'getting' is a link. The question mark marks Kennedy as an example of the party member.
explanation.definitionFit: Kennedy stood for and served as a member of the US party opposed to the Republicans.

clue.text: Ruby? JFK was one of his

definitions.meaning: a ruby is a precious gem, an example of a jewel
the 1991 film JFK was directed by Oliver ...

explanation.surface: Jack Ruby, who shot Oswald, seen as part of the story of JFK.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruby' suggests Jack Ruby, Oswald's killer, but it is the gem; 'JFK' is the film, not the president.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruby is an example of a gem, and the director of the film JFK shares the surname.

clue.text: On frame, is murderee's head movement against revolution

parts.note: re means on, concerning
form means frame or shape

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A frame-up implicating someone, plus a murder victim, set against political upheaval.
explanation.definitionFit: This doctrine favours gradual change within the system rather than overthrowing it by force.

clue.text: Forces one learner, entering American university, to sign

indicators.note: the two letters go into the university's abbreviation

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology
I is the Roman numeral one
L is a learner driver, from the British L-plate
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A student joins an American college and signs up with the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Armies and other armed services are military forces; the plural noun covers several nations' armed services.

clue.text: 9's latest film: great work

indicators.note: the latest letter is the last one

parts.note: the answer to 9 across, a gem or the film director's surname
pic is short for picture, a film

explanation.surface: Oliver Stone's newest movie is hailed as a masterpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 refers to the answer at 9 across, whose final letter is E.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand heroic poem or film on a large scale is a major, ambitious piece of work.

clue.text: Feeling president is upset during Independence Day

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for Independence or Independent

indicators.note: the middle pieces go inside the outer pair

parts.note: Mon is short for Monday, a day of the week

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word over, so it reads upwards

explanation.surface: A sense that the president is unhappy on the Fourth of July.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Independence Day' is not the holiday but two abbreviations, one for each word, which 'during' splits to hold the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A vague sense or notion of something is an impression, as in 'I had the feeling that'.

clue.text: Woman's obsession for the other JFK, here? Politician: "Hard replacing leader of country"

parts.note: JFK airport is in New York, NY
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: the new letter takes the place of the first letter of the country

parts.note: Romania is a country
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A politician's alleged affair, with JFK's reputation as a womaniser in the background.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the other' is British slang for sex. 'replacing leader of' swaps the R of ROMANIA for H to give HOMANIA.
explanation.definitionFit: This term describes excessive sexual desire in a woman, an obsession with sex.

clue.text: Writer of "With American flag, can drape …"

parts.note: to flag something is to mark it

indicators.note: the can is draped around the two letters

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Stars and Stripes draped over a container, as if over a coffin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drape' wraps TIN around W and A to give TWAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Huckleberry Finn wrote under this pen name, so he is a famous American writer.

clue.text: See Zapruder film oddly edited — he might have removed guns?

indicators.note: edited film is cut and reassembled, so these letters are rearranged
take the odd-placed letters, first, third, fifth and so on, across the words

explanation.surface: An invitation to watch the famous home movie of the assassination, suggesting it was doctored to remove a gunman.
explanation.walkthrough: The Zapruder film is the home movie of the assassination. The odd letters of SEEZAPRUDERFILM give SEARDRIM, which 'edited' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes away weapons from others is one who disarms them; the question mark flags the made-up agent noun.

clue.text: Men in station like some bottles of beer?

indicators.note: one word is put inside the other

parts.note: a stop is a station on a line
a crew is a team of men

explanation.surface: Workers at a railway station drinking bottled beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Some beer bottles are closed with a threaded cap rather than a crown cork, so they have this kind of top.

clue.text: Irish carrying container scattered the ashes from this?

indicators.note: the Irish abbreviation holds the rearranged letters inside it
the letters of the word are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: An Irishman carrying an urn from which ashes are scattered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattered' gives NCINERATO from the letters of 'container', which 'carrying' places between the two Irish letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A furnace for burning waste produces ash, so the ashes could come from it.

clue.text: Violent woman 6 — he was shot in Dallas, Jack taken with a shot

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: Jack being taken means captured and carried off, so that letter is removed from the soap character's initials

parts.note: J.R. Ewing was famously shot in the TV soap Dallas
J is the abbreviation for jack in cards
a go is a shot, an attempt

explanation.surface: A woman linked to the Dallas shooting, with Jack (Kennedy) killed.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 looks like a cross-reference to 6 down, but is the Roman numeral VI. Dallas was an American TV soap; 'Who shot J.R.?' was its famous cliffhanger. 'taken' removes the J.
explanation.definitionFit: A fierce, domineering or aggressive woman is a virago, a synonym for a shrew.

clue.text: Oswald primarily left gun outside that's hot

indicators.note: the gun goes outside the two letters

parts.note: the Sten is a British submachine gun

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter

explanation.surface: Oswald left behind a gun that was stolen goods.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sten is a British wartime submachine gun; 'that's' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot is slang for goods recently taken illegally, and so difficult to sell on.

clue.text: In centre of Grassy Knoll, he finally drinks

indicators.note: the last letters go in the middle pair
the centre of the word is its middle letters
finally picks the last letter of each word

explanation.surface: A man on the grassy knoll in Dallas finally having a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The grassy knoll is the slope in Dallas from which some believe a second gunman fired; here it only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Beers are drinks, so the plural nouns are an example of the category.

clue.text: Regime to reduce after this, primarily? Family perish in street …

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of each word

parts.note: kin are family

indicators.note: the word for perish goes in the abbreviation for street

parts.note: die means perish

explanation.surface: A low-carb diet to slim down, followed by a family dying in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs the surface on into 25 across, but the clues are solved separately.
explanation.definitionFit: This low-carbohydrate eating plan is a regimen for losing weight.

clue.text: Aim — line's perfect

parts.note: an idea is an aim or intention
L is short for line; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A target and a line of attack judged flawless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ideal is flawless, matching exactly what is wanted.

clue.text: Flames initially going where the dead end up?

indicators.note: the first letter goes, it is removed

parts.note: burns means flames

explanation.surface: Fire at a cremation, and the final resting place of the dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially going' removes B from BURNS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashes of the cremated are kept in funeral vases, so these vessels are where they end up.

clue.text: … street procession in way, steering car to opening

indicators.note: the way word opens up to take the rearranged letters inside

parts.note: a mode is a way of doing something

indicators.note: the letters are steered into a new order

explanation.surface: A procession of cars along the road, with the president's car steered to an opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steering' gives TORCA from 'car to'; 'in' is a link, and 'opening' is the signal that the way word holds them.
explanation.definitionFit: A parade of motor vehicles through the streets, like Kennedy's in Dallas, is a procession.

clue.text: Finally, losing case, when added up

indicators.note: the outer letters, the case, of the word are taken off

explanation.surface: At last dropping a lawsuit, once all is totalled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing case' removes F and Y, the outer letters of FINALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in total, everything having been counted together.

clue.text: Persuades to take part, needing weapon on board ahead of crime

indicators.note: the weapon comes before the crime

parts.note: the rope is one of the weapons in the board game Cluedo
a sin is a wrongdoing, a crime

explanation.surface: Convincing someone to join in a crime that needs a weapon on board.
explanation.walkthrough: Cluedo (Clue in the US) is a murder-mystery board game whose weapons include the rope.
explanation.definitionFit: To rope someone in is to persuade them to join an activity, an informal idiom.

clue.text: See 6
